span.label: **A PRIMING NULL RESULT, STATED IN THE AUTHORS' OWN VOICE AND NOT BURIED:** `Hence, the first hypothesis was not supported: THE PRIMING of introductory psychology students' metacognition and critical thinking DID NOT POSITIVELY PREDICT their ability to dispel psychological misconceptions. This finding likely indicates that THE PRIME HAD NO EFFECT.` The study powered on two published effects - Swami et al. 2014 d = .46, Gervais & Norenzayan 2012 d = .44 - required N = 119 and recruited N = 184. **Every other priming record I have tagged reports an effect; this one reports its absence.** For a corpus about when priming works, a clean negative is worth more than another positive
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE TWO ESCAPE HATCHES ARE NAMED BY THE AUTHORS THEMSELVES, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING:** `Quotation withheld THIS DIFFERENCE COULD BE BECAUSE DIFFERENT WORDS WERE USED in the treatment prime in this study versus Swami et al.'s study.` A null attributed to word choice **cannot be distinguished from a null attributed to the effect not existing** - and that is the move which makes a priming literature hard to falsify. It is stated here by people running an honest study and reporting their own failure, not by a critic, which is exactly why it is worth having in the corpus verbatim
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **SUPRALIMINAL PRIMING DEFINED ON THE AXIS OF INTENT RATHER THAN VISIBILITY:** `nonconscious activation can be achieved via SUPRALIMINAL PRIMING which involves participants' CONSCIOUS AWARENESS OF THE STIMULI, BUT NOT OF ITS INTENT.` **The participant sees the words and does not know what they are for.** dehaene1998 and holcomb2005 argue about whether the stimulus was SEEN at all; this names the other axis entirely, and a corpus that holds both can tell the two kinds of `unconscious` apart instead of pooling them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE LIMITATION SECTION PUTS THE SAME HATCH IN ONE SENTENCE:** `Quotation withheld.` The words came from the Affective Norms for English Words, chosen to be emotionally neutral, and the authors name that choice as the first limitation of the study. **This is the unfalsifiable residue of any priming null** - the manipulation can always have been the wrong manipulation - and it belongs in the corpus as a tagged limitation rather than as a reason to discount the record
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming —causes→ psychological misconceptions
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.2 — the record marks this weak — **WEIGHT 0.2 AND `no-change`, WHICH ARE SAYING DIFFERENT THINGS AND BOTH ARE NEEDED.** `no-change` is the measured direction: the primed and control groups did not differ. The low weight is the STRENGTH OF THE CLAIM, and it is low because the authors immediately name a reason the manipulation might have failed - `different words were used`. A reader must not take this as evidence that priming does not affect misconceptions; it is evidence that THIS prime did not, in a study powered for d = .45. Recording it as an edge at all is the point: the alternative is that the corpus holds only the literature's successes.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: nonconscious activation —operationalised-as→ supraliminal priming
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — **`CAN BE ACHIEVED VIA` IS THE OPERATIONALISATION AND THE REST OF THE QUOTE IS THE PRICE OF IT.** The construct is nonconscious activation; the procedure is a stimulus the participant consciously sees but whose purpose they do not know. That is a genuinely different claim from the masked-priming records in this corpus, which buy unawareness by making the stimulus unreportable. Weight 0.85 rather than 0.95: the sentence is the paper citing Chartrand & Bargh and Dennis et al. for the method, not establishing it.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming —causes→ metacognition
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.3 — the record marks this weak — **THIS IS THE HYPOTHESISED MECHANISM AND IT WAS NOT SUPPORTED - AND IT CARRIES NO `effect_direction` ON PURPOSE.** The hypothesis predicts an increase; the result is no change. Writing `increases` here would record a prediction as a measurement, and writing `no-change` would put the study's outcome on a row whose quote is its expectation. Q-801 is exactly the ambiguity that makes that dangerous, so the axis is left off and the direction lives on the null edge, where the quote reports a result. Weight 0.3: the relation is the paper's own design assumption, stated plainly, and tested and not found.
